subject: How to use the within_covariates argument?

messages.author: 3cff9fa5ce412dad
messages.subject: How to use the within_covariates argument?
parts:
Hi

First, I want to give a great thumbs up to Mike Lawrence for developing this package. I think its a great intellectual achievement that will make the lives of many people much easier.

Now for the issue I am running into.

I have data from a design with
  • one within categorical predictor (DOMAIN, and
  • one numeric within covariate predictor (DISABILITY).

I am trying to analyze the data using ezANOVA, resulting in the following call and output:


> ezANOVA(data, dv=wr.mean, wid=ss, within=domain, within_covariates=disability)


Warning: Converting "domain" to factor for ANOVA.
Warning: Implementation of ANCOVA in this version of ez is experimental and not yet fully validated. Also, note that ANCOVA is intended purely as a tool to increase statistical power; ANCOVA can not eliminate confounds in the data. Specifically, covariates should: (1) be uncorrelated with other predictors and (2) should have effects on the DV that are independent of other predictors. Failure to meet these conditions may dramatically increase the rate of false-positives.
Warning: Covariate"disability" is numeric and will therefore be fit to a linear effect.
Warning: Collapsing data to cell means. *IF* the requested effects are a subset of the full design, you must use the "within_full" argument, else results may be inaccurate.


$ANOVA
  Effect DFn DFd        F            p p<.05       ges
2 domain   1  13 24.68628 0.0002568626     * 0.2986326


Now, that is not what I expected as I don't get a test for the effect of disability. Running, the following call, I do get said test:

> ezANOVA(data, dv=wr.mean, wid=ss, within=.(domain,disability), within_covariates = disability)
Warning: Converting "domain" to factor for ANOVA.
Warning: "disability" will be treated as numeric.
Warning: Implementation of ANCOVA in this version of ez is experimental and not yet fully validated. Also, note that ANCOVA is intended purely as a tool to increase statistical power; ANCOVA can not eliminate confounds in the data. Specifically, covariates should: (1) be uncorrelated with other predictors and (2) should have effects on the DV that are independent of other predictors. Failure to meet these conditions may dramatically increase the rate of false-positives.
Warning: Covariate"disability" is numeric and will therefore be fit to a linear effect.
Warning: There is at least one numeric within variable, therefore aov() will be used for computation and no assumption checks will be obtained.
$ANOVA
             Effect DFn DFd           F            p p<.05          ges
1            domain   1  13 24.68627945 0.0002568626     * 5.783940e-01
2        disability   1  13  0.00902045 0.9257822161       6.279236e-33
3 domain:disability   1  13  3.02291989 0.1057053261       6.062757e-02

The question is whether I understand the usage of the within_covariates parameter correctly? I think the first call is the intended use but only the second call results in the expected output. Should the covariates be specified twice (in within and within_covariates)?

Any help would be nice.

Best
Dieter

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] How to use the within_covariates argument?
parts:
The version using disability as both a within_covariate variable and a within variable is definitely not appropriate.

You should first use it as a within valuable to look at its main effect if that's of interest to you (ex. to confirm it's having an effect worth covarying-out, though even if p>.05 you could still justify using it as a covariate if there is good prior expectation for an effect) and to check if it has an interaction with domain. If there is an interaction, stop; the interaction prevents you from using disability as a covariate. If there is no interaction, you can do a new anova with disability as a covariate to increase power to detect the effect of domain.
